title: `??=` throws on an array key that is not there.
text: [`lower::Lowering::lower_compound_assignment`] rewrites `$a["k"] ??= $v` into the `$a["k"] = $a["k"] ?? $v` it is spelled out of, and the read that rewrite produces is an ordinary one: `nvs_types::expr::presence`'s `mark_guarded_places` fills `nvs_types::Env::coalesce_guarded` from a `??`'s own left operand and from `isset`/`empty`, never from a compound target, so the read takes `rule:php-migration/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value`'s throw at the one key PHP writes the default into. Every other target is already right — a local, a property, and an element whose key is written — and `docs/reference/tools/30-php-differences.md` lists `??=` among the operators that work as PHP's do. Marking the target's levels guarded is not the fix on its own. The read and the write share one `nvs_types::expr_table::ExprInfo` entry per span, so a guarded intermediate level would drop the `null` that [`lower::Lowering::row_ty_of`] asserts is absent, turning `array<?array<int>> $g; $g["0"]["1"] ??= 5;` from an `E0482` into a panic. What closes this is a read-side mark the write side does not read, which is why it is recorded rather than fixed where it was found. `docs/examples/lang/expressions/and-the-ternary/03-settings-with-their-gaps-filled-in.nvs` is the proof that carries it.
